papers.title: Phylogenomics confirms Palaeoptera monophyly and illuminates the origin of winged insects.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies the neopteran wing-folding mechanism as a singular evolutionary innovation.

papers.title: Positive emotional synchrony and intimacy satisfaction: evidence from a multidimensional assessment.
papers.abstract: Emotional synchrony, as an expression of emotional coordination and coherence, is an important indicator of the quality of intimate relationships. However, few studies have systematically examined valence-related differences in emotional synchrony and their implications for relationship satisfaction, and multidimensional evidence remains limited. In the present research, we employed a multidimensional assessment approach that combined behavioural coding, self-reports, and electroencephalography (EEG) hyperscanning to examine the predictive role of emotional synchrony in relationship satisfaction and the mediating role of self-other overlap during actual interactions. Study 1 revealed that positive emotions played a dominant role in emotional synchrony and directly and positively predicted males' intimacy satisfaction, with self-other overlap serving as a partial mediator. Using self-reports and EEG, Study 2 revealed that emotional synchrony/interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) directly and positively predicted intimacy satisfaction in men, whereas its effect on women's intimacy satisfaction was fully mediated by self-other overlap. In summary, positive emotional synchrony positively predicts intimacy satisfaction, which provides empirical support for the understanding of the behavioural and neural mechanisms underlying emotional synchrony.

papers.title: Growth trajectory and miscarriage diagnosis threshold in early IVF pregnancy: multicenter study.
papers.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterize early-pregnancy ultrasound findings in pregnancies conceived via in-vitro fertilization (IVF) for which gestational age is known precisely based on the date of embryo transfer (ET), and to examine their association with first-trimester pregnancy outcome. METHODS: This was a retrospective multicenter cohort study of fresh- and frozen-cycle IVF pregnancies from 14 centers across England between January 2022 and December 2024, with one center contributing additional data from January 2019 to December 2021. Patients with a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy at the first transvaginal ultrasound scan (≤ 9 + 6 weeks' gestation) after ET were included for analysis of pregnancy outcome. Data collected included the date of ET, embryo stage at transfer, early-pregnancy ultrasound measurements, including crown-rump length (CRL) and mean sac diameter (MSD), and expected gestational age. The endpoint was viability at the 11-14-week dating scan. CRL growth was modeled against gestational age using quadratic regression. The diagnostic performance of a range of gestational-age cut-offs for identifying miscarriage was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value (PPV). RESULTS: A total of 10 009 IVF pregnancies were included, of which 8223 (82.2%) were viable at 11-14 weeks and 1786 (17.8%) were non-viable. A significant difference was found in the distribution of CRL measurements at the first ultrasound scan between pregnancies that were found to be viable and those that were non-viable at the subsequent 11-14-week scan (P < 0.001). papers.title: Parental-couple well-being and relationship stability four years following childbirth: a mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore parents' well-being and relationship stability during pregnancy and four years following childbirth. BACKGROUND: Becoming a parent is a life event that challenges the parental couple and influences their relationship and well-being. METHODS: This mixed-methods exploratory cohort study included 381 parents, followed longitudinally from pregnancy Week 25 to four years postpartum. Data were analysed using the logistic regression of survey data, Kaplan‒Meier estimates and qualitative content analysis. Survey instruments measured sense of coherence (a construct reflecting comprehensibility, manageability and meaningfulness), perceived social support and dyadic relationship quality, referring to the primary relationship between two cohabiting, unrelated adults. RESULTS: After four years, 94% of the parental couples remained in a stable relationship. Greater relationship stability was associated with higher levels of a sense of coherence, stronger perceived social support and higher dyadic relationship quality among both mothers and partners. By four years after childbirth (T6), almost six out of 10 parents (59%) reported that nothing negatively impacted their well-being, indicating a decrease in well-being among the remaining 41% of the parents. Parents experience multidimensional vulnerability in the parental-couple relationship, and their well-being was negatively affected by the unpredictability of everyday life. CONCLUSION: Parents' ability to maintain a sense of coherence, access and receive social support and maintain a high-quality couple relationship is associated with their relationship stability four years after childbirth.

papers.title: From Participants to Partners: A Rapid Scoping Review on the Involvement of Survivors/Victims of Intimate Partner Violence in Research.
papers.abstract: Involving people with lived experience as research partners is becoming more common in other fields (e.g., healthcare), but it is unclear whether this is also the case in intimate partner violence (IPV) research. This rapid scoping review aimed to characterize the extent to which IPV survivors/victims have been involved as research partners in the existing literature. We systematically searched five databases (MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Gender Studies, plus a final search in Google Scholar) for empirical studies published between 2014 and 2024 that involved IPV survivors/victims as more than "study participants" (e.g., involvement in the development of research questions, study design, data collection, data analysis, knowledge translation). A total of 2,596 records were identified, and 27 records met the inclusion criteria. Studies often did not report co-researcher demographic characteristics, making it difficult to fully determine the level of involvement of equity-deserving groups in IPV research teams. The most common participatory models used to guide the involvement of survivors/victims were community-based participatory research and participatory action research. Survivor/victim co-researchers were most commonly involved in research design, developing study materials, data analysis, and knowledge translation/dissemination. There was limited evidence of IPV survivors/victims being engaged as full and equal partners, rather than as collaborators or consultants. The review identified barriers, facilitators, diversity issues, and recommendations for IPV co-research, which can inform the development of guidelines for involving survivors/victims as full and equal members of the research team.

papers.title: The multi-mechanism pathway: quantifying the mediating role of perceived barriers of healthcare access in the relationship between intimate partner violence and antenatal care adherence across 31 sub-Saharan African countries.
Reductions in PTSD symptom clusters among perinatal and postnatal survivors of intimate partner violence participating in the Heartbeats program.
papers.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a leading cause of injury among women, especially during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Experiencing IPV increases the risk of mental health disorders, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). PTSD during the perinatal period is associated with poorer maternal mental health and adverse early child outcomes. Heartbeats (HB) is a hospital-based, community-linked violence intervention program designed to reduce morbidity and mortality among perinatal and postnatal survivors of IPV. HB provides crisis intervention, intensive case management, and counseling to pregnant patients up to 2 years postpartum who have experienced IPV. Given the high burden of mental health concerns in this population, a primary goal of HB is to reduce PTSD symptoms. METHODS: This study was conducted at a Level 1 trauma center. Participants were identified through IPV-related injury presentations, routine hospital screening, or referrals. Seventy-four participants completed the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) at intake (baseline) and 4 months postbaseline (follow-up). Total PTSD and subscale scores were calculated for intrusion (re-experiencing), avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and alterations in arousal and reactivity (hyperarousal). Paired-samples t tests assessed changes from baseline to follow-up. RESULTS: Significant reductions were observed in total PTSD symptoms (M=9.16, SD=23.64, p=0.003) and across all subscales: intrusion (re-experiencing; M=2.76, SD=6.19, p<0.001), avoidance (M=1.18, SD=2.90, p<0.001), negative alterations in cognition and mood (M=3.82, SD=8.83, p<0.001), and alterations in arousal and reactivity (hyperarousal; M=2.33, SD=7.25, p=0.008). CONCLUSIONS: HB program participation was associated with significant reductions in overall PTSD severity and each DSM-5 symptom cluster.
